card.band: 20 h. It is a large decoder with deep dependency chains (SILK and CELT), which makes it long-horizon. A frontier agent usually gets CELT or SILK but not both with bit-close output. A weaker model fails to produce output within the quality threshold. Buckets: SILK, CELT, hybrid, FEC/PLC.
card.cheat: Expected outputs for the hidden streams are not shipped, and libopus is not in the image, so the agent cannot link a library. Generated streams cover cases outside the 12 vectors.
card.grading: Hidden: the other nine bitstreams, stereo and mono variants, plus extra streams made with libopus encoder settings in a sealed verifier. Pass by opus_compare quality threshold per stream, and the score is the fraction passed. Mode-specific streams give partial credit for SILK, CELT and hybrid.
card.reference: libopus (BSD-3-Clause) is the oracle; the reference solution is a clean decoder written for the task and validated on all 12 vectors. It scores 1.
card.source: https://opus-codec.org/testvectors/ (opus_testvectors-rfc8251) @ RFC 8251, normative vectors; libopus v1.5.2 BSD-3-Clause; archive licence not stated
card.task: /app ships the RFC 6716 text and 3 of the 12 sample bitstreams with their expected PCM, plus an opus_compare-style quality-metric tool. Agent writes a decoder from scratch (range decoder, SILK LPC and excitation, CELT MDCT/PVQ/band energy, hybrid mode, PLC and FEC, stereo, resampling) that turns .bit files into 48 kHz PCM.

facts.claim: opus-codec.org/testvectors offers opus_testvectors-rfc8251.tar.gz (and the original opus_testvectors.tar.gz)
RFC 8251 vector set has 12 bitstreams (testvector01 to 12), with .bit inputs unchanged from RFC 6716
RFC 8251 ships two decoded outputs per bitstream (standard and 'm' variant that skips the CELT 180-degree phase shift), 24 .dec files total; grader must pick one set

RFC 6716 says the normative part of the spec is the source in Appendix A and the prose may differ from the reference in ordering or simplification
libopus v1.5.2 release tag exists on GitHub
A public pure-Go Opus decoder exists (darui3018823/opus) and self-reports passing the 12 RFC 8251 vectors; its licence was not checked

v1.kill_reason: Cannot be sealed. The RFC 6716 text the seed ships includes Appendix A, the full normative C reference decoder in base64. An agent can decode, build and match the vectors without writing a decoder. Removing Appendix A leaves prose the RFC says may differ from the reference in ordering or simplification, which makes bit-close output unreachable (K9). Test-vector archive licence is also unstated (K6 risk).

spike_plan.kill_if: Extracted source does not build or fails on several vectors; then re-spike with Appendix A removed from /app and check whether prose-only spec can reach bit-close output (K9 risk).
spike_plan.pass_if: Extracted Appendix A source builds and passes all 12 vectors under opus_compare, which confirms the seal breach and kills the idea as K11.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, fetch the full RFC 6716 text and extract the Appendix A.3 base64 block; decode and untar to get the C source.
Build the extracted decoder with gcc -O2 offline and check it links without libopus.
Decode testvector01-12 .bit files with the built tool.
Compare output to the RFC 8251 .dec files (standard set) using the opus_compare tool from libopus tests/.
Record per-stream pass/fail and confirm the decoder is deterministic across two runs.
Also check whether the 'm' variant .dec set is needed to match any stream.

v1.summary: The Opus decoder idea is well grounded: the 12 RFC 8251 vectors, the libopus v1.5.2 release and the RFC text all exist. It fails the sealing gate because the RFC 6716 Appendix A ships the full normative C decoder, so an agent could extract it and pass without engineering, and the 'clean decoder' reference cannot be sealed by simply deleting that appendix without making bit-exact targets unreachable.
